answers.core: As current the `hit_back_faces` option for a raycast is _only_ applicable to convex collision shapes despite the name indicating it should be available for any arbitrary collision shape (since all closed shapes have a 'negative normal' to the surface). Implementation as an add-on would mean a user must contend with two distinct methods to perform a raycast in 3D space and juggle between them depending on application. This seems overkill for what appears to be a relatively simple implementation.
answers.workaround: Technically yes, but with potentially significant performance impacts that can only be mitigated with reduced fidelity.

title: Allow 3D Raycasts to hit back faces on all convex-type collision shapes
